decision.reason: Alternated replay and rollback can use isolated owners without converting the engine globals; no measured deficit yet justifies the upstream and ABI cost of contexts in one native image.
preserve: one native machine per loaded image
BAD_STATE for a second sequential init
one hardware thread and p6_run_frame only

use_case.operation: Keep main replay A and speculative branch B alive, alternate units, restore A while B is stopped, replay and discard B without durable writes.
controls: same configuration and initial state with different input branches
different configurations and media to expose global contamination
use_case.oracle: Each owner equals its isolated control at every boundary in CPU/chipset/RAM, video/PCM, ticks, media events and overlays; actions on A leave B and its future unchanged.

inventory.risk: Singleton storage and non-atomic reentry guard; lifecycle and validation are owner-sensitive.
Generated handlers, callbacks and pointer tables reach globals transitively; CPU/RAM alone are insufficient.
Distinguish immutable shared tables from owner-specific caches, stale mappings and persistent device state.
Output buffers and host callbacks have lifetimes in addition to serialized state.
Per-host-thread TLS does not isolate two alternating owners on one thread; audit failure cleanup, destructors, reserved registers and heap provenance.

owners: Waterbox loaded flag and CD catalog
inventory.risk: A bridge handle alone cannot provide multi-instance libretro or rebind another owner's pointers.

existing_controls.covers: Native fresh processes and clean reload behaviour, not two simultaneous native owners.
Real sandbox restore/alternation, rejection and new-process scenarios; not native contexts in one image.

subbacklog.deliverable: Specify explicit owner IDs, per-unit command protocol, input/state/media identities, output-buffer lifetime and close/flush policy for A/B. Select existing process and sandbox backends without changing engine ABI.
subbacklog.oracle: No host pointer crosses process/sandbox boundaries; native and Waterbox state formats remain distinct; deterministic command order and missing backend fail explicitly.

subbacklog.deliverable: Keep A/B alive and alternate A1/B1/A2/B2 versus isolated controls, then load invalid firmware/media into B and recreate/dispose B while A remains paused.
subbacklog.oracle: Exact per-unit CPU/chipset/RAM, video/PCM/ticks and overlays; B's failed load cannot change A's saved state or future. BUSY and sequential BAD_STATE remain covered in the original single-image ABI.

subbacklog.deliverable: Rollback A during pending DMA/media/input while B is frozen; continue/discard B and exercise same/new owner restore plus invalid/foreign states and cache poison/reconstruction.
subbacklog.oracle: A's restored future equals its isolated branch; B stays exact before/after A operations. No omitted snapshot bytes or pointer normalization, no writes from discarded branches, no stale callback/cache/allocator references or cross-owner frees.

subbacklog.deliverable: Measure two-owner memory, startup, IPC/activation, snapshot and restore cost on the same declared host/tools; set the user's required budget before choosing a new architecture.
subbacklog.oracle: Repeated raw samples and exact correctness controls; identify a concrete unmet budget of process/sandbox isolation, or retain the postponement. No timing claim follows from this study.

subbacklog.condition: Only if MI-D justifies a same-image native benefit and a new scoped task approves the ownership boundary.
subbacklog.deliverable: Inventory all reachable writable globals/TLS/allocations and one narrow explicit-context prototype; audit generated handlers and adapter ABI, or prove platform loader/dependency isolation before a separate-image alternative.
subbacklog.oracle: Repeat MI-B/C on every proposed backend, verify owner-bound callbacks/heaps/caches and same-thread TLS isolation, measure hot-path overhead and upstream-update conflicts. Keep public single-image guards until a complete separately approved gate; no mass conversion or alternate scheduler.
